oewn-09389659-n.learner: the natural world around us, with its plants, animals, land, and so on.
examples: They went for a long walk in the hills to enjoy nature.

oewn-00594278-v.learner: to accept that someone is what they say they are, or to accept their power and right to rule.
examples: The other nations refused to acknowledge him as king.

oewn-00894219-v.learner: to tell someone that you have received something.
examples: The office acknowledged my letter a week after I sent it.

oewn-00742454-v.learner: to accept something as lawful and valid, so that it must be kept to.
examples: Both sides acknowledged the deed before the judge.

oewn-06033638-n.learner: the average of the values a random quantity can take: add all the values and divide by how many there are.
examples: The expectation of one roll of a fair die is 3.5.

oewn-01108582-s.learner: meaning only the thing named itself, and nothing beyond it.
examples: The airport is ten miles outside the city proper.

oewn-02241406-v.learner: to let someone join a group or community.
examples: The club voted to admit two new members.

oewn-02454712-v.learner: to let someone take part in something or have the right to belong to it, with the rights, work, and duties that go with it.
examples: After passing her exams she was admitted to the medical profession.

oewn-02677068-v.learner: to be the thing that lets a person get in.
examples: This ticket admits one adult to the show.

oewn-02747557-v.learner: to lead into a place, or give a way in to it.
examples: The side door admits onto a narrow lane.

oewn-00983916-n.learner: the work of collecting information about an enemy.
examples: The war was partly won through intelligence carried out behind enemy lines.

oewn-08356381-n.learner: a group whose job is to collect information about an enemy and work out what it means.
examples: Military intelligence warned the general that an attack was coming.

oewn-13530399-n.learner: a slow fall in the amount of something, or in how much activity there is.
examples: The town saw a steady loss of trade over ten years.

oewn-07302177-n.learner: the experience of losing someone you love.
examples: She was still grieving the loss of her mother.

oewn-13348253-n.learner: the amount by which what a business spends is more than what it earns.
examples: The shop made a loss of five hundred pounds last year.

oewn-07348249-n.learner: a gentle way of saying someone's death.
examples: News of the old doctor's loss spread quickly through the village.

oewn-07355325-n.learner: soldiers and other military people lost because they were killed or captured.
examples: The army suffered heavy losses in the battle.

oewn-04966407-n.learner: a form of a colour that is slightly different from another.
examples: The walls were painted in soft tones of green.

oewn-04994869-n.learner: the special quality of a sound, such as a voice, a noise, or music, that makes it different from other sounds.
examples: The old violin has a warm, rich tone.

oewn-06878395-n.learner: a written sign in music that shows how high a sound is and how long it lasts.
examples: Each tone was written on the page as a small black mark.

oewn-14568274-n.learner: the natural firmness of living muscles, blood vessels, and similar parts that helps them respond when something acts on them.
examples: Regular swimming improves muscle tone.

oewn-06872106-n.learner: in music, a gap in pitch equal to two half steps.
examples: From C up to D is one tone.

oewn-05727552-n.learner: a steady sound with no other sounds mixed into it.
examples: The machine gave out a single high tone.

oewn-04994132-n.learner: the height of the voice, or a change in it, that makes one word different from another in languages that work this way.
examples: In Mandarin, the same sound said with a different tone can be a different word.

oewn-05826885-n.learner: facts that someone has learned by watching or noticing things.
examples: The scientist's observations showed that the birds left in October.

oewn-01004898-n.learner: the act of measuring something and writing down the result.
examples: Weather observations are taken every hour at the station.

oewn-05881589-n.learner: a general statement that describes facts or events that happen again and again in nature.
examples: An apple falls to the ground because of the law of gravity.

oewn-08226608-n.learner: the police, as a body of officers.
examples: He had been running from the law for years.

oewn-05879538-n.learner: a rule, or a set of rules, about how to behave that comes from human nature and that human society needs and must follow.
examples: He argued that the law of nature forbids cruelty to the weak.

oewn-06171434-n.learner: the part of philosophy that studies law and the ideas that lead courts to decide as they do.
examples: In her philosophy class she studied law and asked why judges decide as they do.
